---
title: "MAR"
description: "Generate diverse mixtures of autoregressive processes and target time-series features."
---

`MARGenerator` draws mixture autoregressive (MAR) series for foundation-model
pretraining. At each time step it selects an autoregressive component and uses
that component's intercept, lag coefficients, and innovation scale:

$$
y_t = c_k + \sum_{i=1}^{p_k} \phi_{k,i} y_{t-i} + \sigma_k \varepsilon_t.
$$

The mixture autoregressive model is due to
[Wong and Li (2000)](https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9868.00222); the
breadth-oriented sampling recipe follows
[GRATIS](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.02787). SynForecast samples stationary
coefficients through partial autocorrelations and adds bounded retries,
optional seasonal AR factors, and explicit output standardization.

## Generate a diverse MAR pool

Random mode samples a new configuration for every series. `seasonal_period`
enables a seasonal AR factor for a random subset of components.

```python
from synforecast.generators import MARGenerator

generator = MARGenerator(
    min_length=168,
    max_length=336,
    freq="h",
    max_components=4,
    max_ar_order=6,
    seasonal_period=24,
    seed=42,
)

mar_df = generator.generate(n_series=1_000, n_jobs=-1)
```

Bulk `generate()` calls use the native Rust batch path and are deterministic
for a fixed seed regardless of worker count. The native and Python reference
paths implement the same model contract but use different RNG streams, so do
not compare `generate()` output bit-for-bit with successive
`generate_single_series()` calls.

By default each accepted series is standardized to population mean zero and
standard deviation one. Set `standardize=False` when component-implied levels
and scales are part of the desired distribution.

## Supply a fixed MAR model

Fixed mode is enabled by supplying all four fixed fields together. Every AR
component must be stationary and the mixture must be second-order stationary
(Wong and Li 2000); weights are normalized during validation. `seasonal_period`
has no effect in fixed mode. A fixed model whose simulation fails the finite,
bounded, non-constant output guards raises a `ValueError` instead of silently
returning noise.

```python
fixed = MARGenerator(
    min_length=256,
    max_length=256,
    freq="D",
    weights=[0.65, 0.35],
    ar_coefficients=[[0.8], [0.35, -0.15]],
    intercepts=[0.0, 0.5],
    noise_scales=[0.4, 1.2],
    standardize=False,
    seed=7,
)

fixed_df = fixed.generate(n_series=20)
```

`weights`, `ar_coefficients`, `intercepts`, and `noise_scales` are an
all-or-nothing group. Leaving all four unset selects random mode.

## Target time-series features

`tune_to_features` searches for one fixed MAR configuration whose realized
features approach a target. Supported features are `spectral_entropy`,
`trend_strength`, `seasonal_strength`, and `acf1`.

```python
targeted = MARGenerator.tune_to_features(
    target_features={"acf1": 0.75, "spectral_entropy": 0.45},
    min_length=96,
    max_length=192,
    freq="D",
    n_generations=15,
    population_size=30,
    n_draws_per_candidate=3,
    seed=42,
)

targeted_df = targeted.generate(n_series=100)
print(targeted.tuning_diagnostics)
```

Candidate fitness is averaged over deterministic lengths spanning the requested
range, and feature computation runs in Rust. Targets describe a distribution,
not an exact per-series constraint: evaluate the realized feature distribution
at the lengths and seeds used downstream. Seasonal-strength targeting also
requires `seasonal_period` and at least two complete periods at `min_length`.

::: {.callout-note}
The search evaluates at most the product of `n_generations`,
`population_size`, and `n_draws_per_candidate` simulated paths, stopping early
once the best L2 feature distance is at or below `tolerance` (default `0.05`).
Infeasible targets return the best candidate found within that fixed budget.
`tuning_diagnostics` reports `best_distance`, `converged`, `generations_run`,
and `candidates_evaluated`. The distance is the selected candidate's observed
search fitness; evaluate fresh draws to measure performance on new samples.
:::

## When to use MAR

Use MAR when you want many stationary or seasonally autoregressive shapes from
a compact model family, or when a pretraining corpus needs controlled coverage
of autocorrelation and entropy. For decomposed trend/seasonal/irregular
compositions use [TSI](tsi); for random causal graphs and nonlinear lead-lag
structure use [TCM](tcm); for Gaussian-process kernel compositions use
[KernelSynth](kernel_synth).

Full constructor parameters are listed in the
[generator reference](https://github.com/Nixtla/synforecast/blob/main/GENERATORS.md).
